access.edition_or_version: First edition, Farrar, Straus and Cudahy (1959); National Book Award 1960

mechanics.tone_relevance: Origin point of the 'confessional' label: M. L. Rosenthal's 1959 review described the poet as removing the mask and offering personal confidences.
mechanics.point_of_view: First person speaker identified with the poet; autobiographical material (marriage, illness, family) disclosed directly.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Family history and personal breakdown are disclosed across the collection, moving from remembered youth to adult crisis.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Loose, conversational meters and colloquial diction against earlier formal verse; prose memoir section ('91 Revere Street'); concrete domestic detail.
mechanics.register: Casual and colloquial; the downward register shift is the signature of the new confessional mode.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: The speaker is 'unequivocally himself'; the reader is positioned as the recipient of confidences.
mechanics.critical_reception: Widely credited with inaugurating the confessional poetry movement; also the target of the charge that disclosed interiority is self-dramatisation rather than craft.
mechanics.copyright_note: Poems copyrighted. Techniques and reception described, no text reproduced.
